d: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Canonical is globally expanding its Embedded Devices Software Solution Sales team, hiring managers, directors, and account managers to broaden reach in mission-critical industries. The successful candidates will focus on our Ubuntu product portfolio, which is already widely used in connected devices and industrial PCs. Our newer offering, Ubuntu Core for IoT, provides state-of-the-art security and resilience for high-end appliances and equipment, serving global brands in consumer, industrial electronics, automotive, and robotics. We are continually enhancing this portfolio with features like real-time Linux capability and pursuing various certifications, representing Linux reinvented for optimal reliability, security, developer productivity, and footprint. We seek technically skilled professionals familiar with embedded Linux and RTOS.

This is a high-energy role focused on prospecting sales and strategic account development, demanding ambition and focus. You will be responsible for carrying an annual bookings quota and must be comfortable positioning and selling a range of open source, services, and software solutions. Leveraging Ubuntu's market adoption, the work requires actively building trusted and profitable commercial relationships, developing the potential of your territory beyond managing inbound interest. This involves prospecting new business, maintaining existing relationships, and working with colleagues on account strategy. Candidates must be effective in selling complex technical solutions, including enterprise software, cloud, virtualization, and container technologies, to senior levels of the enterprise and departments focused on embedded software and IoT devices. Professional practice, clear account planning, continuous pipeline reporting, and the ability to travel regionally for client engagement and internationally for company events twice a year are expected.
Location: We are growing our sales reach with remote roles in all regions - EMEA, APAC, and Americas; and office based roles in Taipei, Taiwan.
Building and executing a territory sales plan to prioritize leading security-focused brands and manufacturers
Working with marketing to promote our brand and increase market awareness in prioritized accounts
Developing pipeline through outreach, prospecting, local marketing, and industry events
Closing contracts to meet and exceed quarterly and annual bookings targets and achieve strategic objectives
Managing customer relationships and interactions through all stages of the sales cycle
Working with Field Engineers to understand customer requirements and ensure customer satisfaction
Maintaining accurate data and forecasts within Salesforce
Establishing productive professional relationships with key influencers and decision-makers
Coordinating with colleagues, including support, delivery, and management
q: Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
Undergraduate degree in a technical subject
Confidence to respectfully speak up, exchange feedback, and share ideas without hesitation
Track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results
Field sales experience in embedded Linux, embedded software, or enterprise software
Track record of achievement of sales targets and large account wins
Professional written and spoken English with excellent presentation skills
Experience with Linux (Debian or Ubuntu preferred)
Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability
Result-oriented, with a personal drive to meet commitments

In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. d: The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. Our research and policy advice help governments, businesses, communities, and civil society make better decisions. Our international Energy Program works with partners across countries and disciplines.
We are currently looking for a Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, to work within the IISD Energy Program.

The Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, will work within IISD’s International Strategy team, helping governments and partners advance a Paris-aligned, just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuel production and consumption, including reform of fossil fuel subsidies and public finance. We recognize the difficult choices facing fossil-fuel-dependent economies: protecting public revenues, energy security, jobs, and affordability while building more resilient and diversified economies. The role involves close collaboration with government counterparts, particularly in the Global South, and with researchers, intergovernmental organizations, and civil society, as well as other teams within IISD’s 50-staff Energy Program and other Institute programs.

The Policy Advisor will help design and implement applied research, policy advice, and technical assistance for countries seeking practical transition pathways. For example, the work may examine the effects of changing fossil fuel revenues on government budgets, assess subsidy reform options, or help translate national and international transition commitments into implementable measures. Key responsibilities include
q: A bachelor’s degree or equivalent in economics, public finance, development studies, public policy, natural resource management or a related field. A relevant master’s or PhD degree is an advantage.
At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in macroeconomic or fiscal policy, applied economic research, public finance, energy policy, or fossil fuel transitions.
Strong strategic thinking, with examples of turning broad questions into concrete outputs and delivering projects to a high standard.
A sound understanding of the economic and fiscal implications of energy transition, particularly for countries dependent on fossil fuel production, revenues, or consumption subsidies.
Experience engaging government or public-policy stakeholders, preferably in emerging or developing economies, with sensitivity to local institutions, data and policy priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce concise, persuasive policy notes or proposals for non-specialist audiences.
Proven project management: able to scope work, assign and follow up on responsibilities, manage deadlines, and flag risks early in international, multi-partner settings.
Experience providing constructive feedback, reviewing colleagues’ work or supporting the development of less experienced team members; formal line-management experience is not required.
A proactive and accountable working style: able to work independently, prioritize realistically, seek clarification early, and follow through reliably on commitments.
Resourcefulness and sound judgement about data and methods, including when to use government data, partner expertise, or specialist modelling rather than assuming one tool fits every task.
A collaborative, respectful approach across cultures and professional perspectives, with openness to feedback and a commitment to shared learning.
Excellent oral and written English. Proficiency in another language will be considered an advantage.
The successful applicant could also have (desirable)
Experience in fundraising or preparing successful proposals, including translating funder feedback into clearer project design.
Applied experience in fossil fuel subsidy reform, public financial flows, economic diversification, transition planning or government-facing technical assistance.
Experience working with quantitative economic or energy-sector data or supervising specialist analytical work. Applicants with additional relevant experience who value hands-on delivery are welcome.

Location: Remote, based in one of the following eligible Global South countries where IISD can employ staff: Burkina Faso, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Philippines, Qatar, Rwanda, South Africa, or Uganda; or hybrid in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. The role involves regular online collaboration with colleagues and partners based in Europe and the East Coast of the Americas; reasonable overlap with agreed team meeting hours is required.
Candidates must hold appropriate work authorization in the country they are based in without any sponsorship from IISD.
Salary: Salary commensurate with experience and location.
Employment type: 80%–100% full-time-equivalent staff position, under an Employer of Record model.
This is a 1-year contractual position with a possibility of extension.
Start Date: As soon as feasible
All submissions must be in English.
Applications will only be accepted through Bamboo HR.
A CV (no longer than two pages)
Applications without a cover letter or CV will not be considered. Please include your availability and salary expectations in your CV.
Only those candidates we wish to interview will be contacted. Resumes will be kept on file for 1 year.

IISD is committed to fostering a more equitable and sustainable world and welcomes candidates who uphold our values of diversity, equity, and inclusion. We encourage applications from individuals from historically underrepresented and marginalized communities, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, people of diverse racial and ethnic identities, and people of diverse sexual orientations, gender identities, gender expressions, and/or sex characteristics (SOGIESC).

We are committed to equitable and inclusive recruitment practices and to reducing barriers to employment and advancement. Hiring decisions are based on qualifications, experience, competencies, and organizational needs, while recognizing the value that diverse perspectives and lived experiences bring to our work. We offer reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process and welcome applicants’ input on how best to support their participation. Candidates are invited to voluntarily self-identify and complete our employment equity questionnaire through our applicant tracking system
r: Leading policy-oriented research and analysis on fossil fuel transitions, public financial flows, macroeconomic and fiscal risks, subsidies, energy security and economic diversification; translating evidence into actionable options for decision-makers.

Designing and managing assigned workstreams and outputs, with clear workplans, responsibilities, quality checks, and milestones; coordinating partners; and contributing to reporting and budget management alongside financial project managers.

Building trusted relationships with government counterparts, especially in fossil fuel-dependent economies, as well as knowledge organizations, civil society networks and intergovernmental partners; adapting support to country needs and available evidence.
Supporting the development of more junior colleagues through clear task briefs, constructive feedback, peer review, and learning by doing.
Contributing to focused funding proposals and partner engagement that build on demonstrated demand and the team’s existing expertise.
Working with IISD Communications early in the process to turn research into clear, useful messages and products for intended audiences.

We are looking for a thoughtful, self-directed policy professional who combines analytical rigour with practical judgement and reliable delivery. The successful applicant can turn a complex policy question into a workable plan, communicate trade-offs clearly, and work constructively with colleagues across disciplines and time zones. They will understand that fossil fuel-dependent countries face real fiscal, political, and development constraints and will seek credible, country-owned transition solutions rather than one-size-fits-all prescriptions. This is a hands-on role with opportunities to take growing ownership and help develop colleagues.

d: The Site Engineer is responsible for ensuring that all construction activities comply with the project's technical specifications, quality standards, safety regulations, and scheduled timelines.
Interpret and monitor project drawings and specifications to ensure construction activities align with contract requirements and Ministry/industry standards.
Assist in developing method statements and ensure adherence to approved methodologies during execution.
Ensure accurate survey control is established and maintained to ensure works are constructed to the correct line and level, in coordination with surveyors.
Verify that all materials used on-site comply fully with project specifications.
Monitor daily construction activities against approved drawings, specifications and project schedules
Prepare and submit inspection requests to the consultant and coordinate required inspections
Coordinate with utility authorities and relevant stakeholders before commencing excavation and diversion works
Monitor earthworks, compaction tests, concrete tests, asphalt testing and other required quality tests
Coordinate with specialist subcontractors, and the supply of materials and equipment.
Optimize resource usage and minimize material wastage to enhance project profitability.
Plan and organize work efficiently to meet project deadlines and milestones.
Ensure that all construction activities are carried out in accordance with approved method statements and ITPs
Identify site constraints, technical issues and discrepancies in drawings and coordinate timely resolution
Promote and maintain a safe and healthy work environment in compliance with safety regulations.
Monitor subcontractor performance, manpower productivity and equipment utilisation
Maintain daily site diaries and provide accurate progress reports to the Senior Engineer.
Perform additional duties as assigned by management.
Ensure that completed works are properly measured, recorded and reflected in as-built drawings
Carry out regular inspections of temporary works, including formwork, shoring, excavation support and other temporary structures, when appointed as Temporary Works Coordinator.
Bachelors degree in Civil Engineering or Diploma in Civil Engineering
Minimum 3-5 years’ experience in the construction industry working for a Contractor, with Bahrain or GCC experience preferably

Experience in a site engineer role on new road infrastructure projects including technical responsibility for asphalt laying, road base, sub-base, kerbstones, paving, drainage installation and utility reinstatement and diversions
Demonstrated effective communication, and sound decision-making abilities
Proficient in a range of computer applications relevant to engineering and project management
